items.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

ctx.x: So, being a studio musician, you go to work in the studio—

Well it was all freelance when I — just when I got into it, they had contracts. Up until then, where they had house bands, all studios had their own group. And during that period I was doing radio. I did “The Phil Harris Show,” and I’m trying to think of what shows I did, and I started to do records, and there was also quotas, if you did movie studio work, you could only do a certain number of records, you couldn’t do radio at all I don’t think. They tried to divide up the work among all. So I was like in that…
Did this give you any — this is like a 90s question — did you get health benefits and all that kind of stuff for that kind of work?
